headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via shared files; Superset is read-only while Unstructured can read/write and parse documents.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress, while Unstructured can read/write files and parse documents. If Superset outputs are saved into a shared workspace, Unstructured may ingest attacker-controlled content as trusted text. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF Superset outputs are written into a shared directory that Unstructured reads
IF Unstructured treats document text as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Separate input/output directories for the two agents
Disable automatic ingestion of Superset-generated files
Add a manual review step before Unstructured processes any Superset output
Use file naming conventions that mark untrusted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files and reject untrusted sources by policy

B_data_leakage.rationale: Superset is a data-engineering tool with API access and allowlisted egress; Unstructured reads documents and can write files. If both touch the same workspace, document contents can flow from shared files into Unstructured processing and then out through its networked pipeline. No sensitive class is explicitly listed, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or workspace
IF documents processed by Unstructured contain sensitive material
mitigations: Store each agent’s files in separate directories
Restrict Unstructured to non-sensitive sample documents
Turn off network access for Unstructured during sensitive runs
Review Superset exports before handing them to Unstructured
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs between the agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Superset has API access and Unstructured can read/write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and supports multiple instances. Overlap on mutable files can create write conflicts even without explicit git or DB state. Because the shared mutable surface is plausible but not directly documented, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF either agent mutates shared artifacts without locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Use lock files around shared artifacts
Make outputs append-only where possible
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutexes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Superset can produce analytics outputs, and Unstructured can transform documents; if Unstructured consumes Superset output without verification, errors or hallucinated structure can cascade into downstream artifacts. The pair lacks documented verification boundaries, so the interaction is plausible but indirect, warranting medium.
conditions: IF Unstructured ingests Superset-generated text as authoritative input
IF no human or automated verification step exists between them
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on Superset outputs
Flag low-confidence fields for manual review
Keep Unstructured outputs non-authoritative until checked
requires-engineering: add automated consistency tests

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source with docs-only evidence and no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is stated. Superset lists no data classes touched, while Unstructured touches documents/images/text and exposes a privacy-policy URL. With no documented mismatch, only a small compliance gap is plausible, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through Unstructured
IF the operator relies on a retention or residency guarantee not documented here
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Review the privacy policy before deployment
Document retention expectations internally
Keep audit logs of processed document classes
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance attestations
